title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling for legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the briefing says Microsoft documents no way to include or exclude individual legacy file formats, but the cited documentation already describes file-extension conditions and exceptions. Narrow that statement to the undocumented legacy-format rollout behavior rather than implying that policies have no file-type filtering.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans server-side auto-labeling support for Word .doc, Excel .xls and PowerPoint .ppt files.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview server-side auto-labeling will support legacy Microsoft Office file formats, including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt).

claims.claim: The planned capability evaluates and applies sensitivity labels to files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Organizations can automatically evaluate and apply sensitivity labels to these files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy reaches policy activation.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy ... When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -Mode Enable enables an auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: The Mode parameter specifies the action and notification level of the auto-labeling policy. Valid values are: Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: TestWithoutNotifications is the policy's test mode.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations where you want to apply the label reaches location selection.
claims.quote: For a policy in the Off section, select the Edit policy button. ... For the page Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -AddSharePointLocation "<site URL>" adds a SharePoint site to policy locations.
claims.quote: The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the SharePointLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: AddOneDriveLocation is the corresponding parameter for adding OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no setting that includes or excludes .doc, .xls or .ppt files individually.
claims.quote: Other conditions that you can select: Attachment or file extension is ... Depending on your previous choices, you'll now have an opportunity to create new rules by using conditions and exceptions.

Keep the existing cited URL https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
